name: SWE-bench
environment: Real GitHub repositories pinned to fixed commits and terminal containers
verifier: FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests
main_limit: Public issues and patches are prone to contamination; hidden tests may underspecify a task or reject equivalent fixes

name: SWE-bench Pro
environment: Longer-horizon tasks in real repositories with containerized execution
verifier: Task tests and regression tests
main_limit: Environment setup and test quality still introduce infrastructure confounds, and public tasks have a short half-life

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
environment: Isolated CLI containers spanning multiple classes of system tasks
verifier: Per-task unit or integration tests
main_limit: Hardware, network, and container configuration can substantially change scores; the benchmark does not close the rules of any single industry

name: Cybench
environment: Kali Linux and CTF targets
verifier: Final flags and human-annotated subtasks
main_limit: The CTF distribution differs from real offensive operations, and flag-based scoring may hide unintended exploit paths

name: CyberGym
environment: Pre- and post-patch versions of historical vulnerable codebases in isolated execution environments
verifier: Differential crash oracle that triggers before but not after the patch
main_limit: Deployment is expensive and requires strict network isolation; a single crash condition does not establish a valid or complete exploit chain

name: CVE-Bench
environment: Forty real critical web CVEs in isolated attack sandboxes
verifier: Execution outcomes such as denial of service, file or database access, remote execution, and unauthorized login
main_limit: High-risk exploit execution requires strict isolation; a single outcome predicate may admit unintended paths, and version changes can alter task semantics

name: Finance Agent Benchmark
environment: Web, SEC EDGAR, and computation tools
verifier: Expert answers, atomic rubrics, model judges, and citation checks
main_limit: Covers research retrieval and computation rather than the full trading, approval, and regulatory workflow; results depend on rubric completeness

name: FinToolBench
environment: 760 executable financial tools and 295 mandatory-tool queries
verifier: Execution success plus alignment with recency, intent type, and regulatory domain
main_limit: Runnable tools do not reproduce institutional permissions, approvals, or market state; the ecosystem requires continuous maintenance for freshness and availability

name: BigFinanceBench
environment: Retrieval and computation tasks modeled on real financial-research workflows
verifier: Auditable retrieval, definition, and calculation derivations
main_limit: Outputs remain largely question-answer deliverables; market recency, institutional conventions, and writes to real state are only weakly covered

name: MedAgentBench
environment: FHIR-compatible virtual EHRs, patient records, and read/write tools
verifier: Assertions over FHIR resources and terminal patient state
main_limit: Simulated records and rewards require ongoing clinical audit and cannot support claims about real hospital permissions, liability, or patient outcomes

name: AgentClinic
environment: Simulated patients, diagnostic tools, and multimodal clinical information
verifier: Diagnostic accuracy, patient-centered measures, and a reader study
main_limit: The patient simulator is itself part of the measurement system, and diagnostic endpoints do not cover treatment safety or real outcomes

name: CHI-Bench (χ-Bench)
environment: Twenty healthcare applications, 87 MCP tools, policy manuals, and cross-role workflows
verifier: Workflow terminal states, artifacts, and policy checks
main_limit: Simulated organizations, policy coverage, and irreversible actions still require human and production calibration before safety claims can transfer

name: HealthAgentBench
environment: Fifty-four tasks across seven environment types covering EHRs, imaging, trial matching, and data engineering
verifier: Task success, runtime, and cost
main_limit: A unified terminal score obscures differences among task classes, and terminal environments cannot replace clinical supervision, patient outcomes, or real permissions

name: HealthBench
environment: Multiturn, multilingual health conversations without writable clinical state
verifier: Physician-authored, conversation-level weighted rubrics with a calibrated model judge
main_limit: Measures health communication and safe responses rather than EHR agency; open-ended grading remains sensitive to rubric and judge bias

name: LegalAgentBench
environment: Seventeen legal corpora, 37 tools, and 300 tasks
verifier: Answer keywords and intermediate progress rate
main_limit: Keyword scoring cannot capture equivalent legal arguments or legal validity, and the benchmark mainly targets Chinese legal retrieval and writing

name: Harvey Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB)
environment: Closed client matters, files, emails, and templates
verifier: Lawyer-authored atomic rubrics with all critical items required
main_limit: Deliverable evaluation is strong but programmable state is limited; expert rubrics, material licensing, and run protocols are still evolving

name: MLE-bench
environment: Seventy-five Kaggle competitions with data, GPU, and code environments
verifier: Competition metrics and medal thresholds
main_limit: Kaggle rank depends on compute and historical priors and does not represent open-ended research innovation or production deployment

name: PaperBench
environment: Twenty papers, code containers, and fresh reproduction environments
verifier: 8,316 hierarchical outcomes, JudgeEval, and fresh reproduction
main_limit: Hierarchical rubrics and reruns are expensive, and reproducing existing papers is not equivalent to proposing new research

name: RE-Bench
environment: Seven frontier AI R&D task environments under fixed time budgets
verifier: Continuous task scores and time-matched human baselines
main_limit: The task set is small and resource matching is difficult; short-horizon advantages do not imply multiday research adaptation

name: τ-bench
environment: Airline and retail databases, policies, tools, and a user simulator
verifier: Target database state, dialogue and policy assertions, and pass^k
main_limit: User-simulator bias and fixed policy templates limit transfer, while terminal-state checks may miss process violations

name: τ²-bench
environment: Dual-control environments such as telecom in which both user and agent change state
verifier: Environment terminal state, communication and policy assertions, and repeated reliability
main_limit: Simulated-user cooperativeness materially changes scores, leaving a sim-to-real gap to actual customer behavior

name: τ³-bench
domain: Customer service, knowledge, and voice workflows
environment: Retail, airline, telecom, and banking environments with roughly 700 knowledge-base documents and real-time voice interaction
verifier: Environment terminal state, retrieval, communication and policy assertions, and repeated reliability
main_limit: Knowledge and voice improve interaction realism, but the user model, acoustic conditions, task version, and scoring configuration must all be pinned

name: WorkArena++
environment: ServiceNow enterprise SaaS with compositional workflows
verifier: Programmatic setup and validation plus oracle traces
main_limit: Coverage is concentrated on one platform and a designer-defined task grammar; a large number of combinations does not guarantee structural diversity

name: CRMArena-Pro
environment: Salesforce-style CRM with B2B and B2C scenarios, roles, and multiturn users
verifier: CRM state queries, task success, and confidentiality checks
main_limit: Simulated business data and personas differ from real organizations, and confidentiality instructions can trade off against task completion

name: AppWorld
environment: Nine simulated applications, 457 APIs, and resettable databases
verifier: Target-state tests and collateral-damage checks
main_limit: State verification is strong but there is no single industry policy layer, and simulated apps omit production permissions and API drift

name: GDPval
environment: File-based professional deliverable tasks from 44 occupations
verifier: Paired preferences from industry experts or comparison with reference deliverables
main_limit: One-shot deliverables do not establish a multiday loop, and expert preference may entangle factual, procedural, and formatting errors

name: APEX-Agents
environment: Cross-application workspaces, files, and tools for investment banking, consulting, and corporate law
verifier: Binary atomic rubrics, gold outputs, and execution trajectories
main_limit: The benchmark decomposes deliverable quality but does not reproduce multiday organizational processes, real client permissions, or final business outcomes

name: SpreadsheetBench 2
environment: 321 real multi-sheet business tasks covering generation, debugging, and visualization
verifier: Workbook execution and task accuracy under a shared agent scaffold
main_limit: Spreadsheet work is a function rather than an industry loop, and formula recalculation, application versions, and task templates affect reproducibility

name: WebArena
environment: Self-hosted websites, a browser, and resettable state
verifier: Programmatic evaluators over URLs, DOM, and database state
main_limit: Primarily measures browser control rather than industry rules, and self-hosted templates differ from a drifting live web

name: VisualWebArena
environment: Self-hosted websites with visual content and a browser
verifier: Web-state and visual-task evaluators
main_limit: Visual grounding is stronger, but the benchmark remains interface evidence rather than a vertical industry loop and covers a limited website distribution

name: OSWorld
environment: Real operating systems, desktop applications, and restorable virtual machines
verifier: 134 classes of execution-based evaluators
main_limit: Results are sensitive to environment versions, resolution, and application state, while interface success does not establish domain-policy compliance

name: AndroidWorld
environment: Resettable Android emulators and native applications
verifier: Checks over application databases, files, or UI state
main_limit: Focuses on mobile UI skill, with gaps between emulator and device behavior and sensitivity to application versions

name: TheAgentCompany
environment: Enterprise websites, code repositories, chat, and colleague agents
verifier: Task-specific program checks with partial deliverable evaluation
main_limit: The organizational model and colleague behavior are simplified simulations, and cross-application work is not automatically an industry vertical

name: InterCode
environment: Code interpreters, SQL, and shell interaction environments
verifier: Execution results, tests, or target state
main_limit: Provides a general interaction threshold without specialized domain knowledge, policy, or governance

name: ToolSandbox
environment: Stateful, multiturn simulated tools with implicit dependencies
verifier: Milestone similarity and final-state checks
main_limit: Cross-domain tool capability is strong but domain rules are shallow, and simulated tools still differ from real API behavior

name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
environment: Multiple classes of function schemas and executable calling tasks
verifier: AST, execution, and state-based scoring
main_limit: Measures general function calling rather than a vertical loop, and leaderboard versioning and format adaptation affect comparisons

name: MCP-Atlas
environment: Thirty-six version-pinned real MCP servers, more than 220 tools, and containerized environments
verifier: Claim coverage, expected tool calls, and error diagnosis
main_limit: An LLM judge and claim rubric do not establish business terminal state; services, credential requirements, and scorer versions can change results

name: FinanceBench
environment: Public company filings and finance questions
verifier: Expert answers and supporting evidence spans
main_limit: Static QA has no tool state or action consequences and serves only as a financial knowledge and retrieval threshold

name: LegalBench
environment: Multiple legal understanding and reasoning datasets
verifier: Classification, generation, or task-specific static metrics
main_limit: There is no persistent environment or executable legal workflow, so high scores do not establish the ability to deliver legal services
